the nature of visitors’ experiences of cultural tourism.
the nature and extent of the cultural tourism product and how it is experienced by visitors.
how people experience cultural tourism.

the Maori Arts & Crafts Institute provides an entertaining and educational experience that is a “must see” for tourists visiting New Zealand.
the Maori Arts & Crafts Institute is a popular site, but one that is visited primarily for its entertainment and educational value, rather than as a cultural experience.
the experience of visiting a site such as the Maori Arts Institute is one that is largely functional and that the cultural component of the experience is largely a peripheral one.

the majority of visitors to the Maoris Arts and Crafts Institute visit because it is a “done-thing” when visiting New Zealand, and they are satisfied with the experience.
visitors are not necessarily seeking a “Maori experience” per se but are more interested in the experience of visiting a Maori site.

, whereas cultural tourism is a significant industry worldwide, it is often not the cultural component of the experience which is of most importance to the visitor.
the visitor experience is a complex one, with multiple motivations and outcomes.
